sentences.text: Sanjuansaurus was roughly the size of a medium Herrerasaurus, possessing a femur measuring exactly 395 mm and a tibia measuring exactly 360 mm.

Unlike other herrerasaurids, the pubis of this animal pointed toward the cranium, and it was relatively short, measuring 63% of the femur length with a pronounced rugose scar on the medial surface of the femur at the fourth trochanter.

Its skeleton featured shelf-like transverse processes on cervical vertebrae, acute anterior and posterior processes on the sixth to eighth dorsal neural spines, and everted lateral margins on the glenoid.
The pubis of Sanjuansaurus points toward the cranium, a trait unlike that found in other herrerasaurids.
The species name S. gordilloi was named in honor of Raúl Gordillo, the main fossil preparator and artist at the San Juan Museum.
Sanjuansaurus was named and described in 2010 by Oscar Alcober and Ricardo Martinez, following its discovery in 1994 by paleontologist Ricardo N. Martínez.
The holotype skeleton, catalogued as PVSJ 605, was unearthed in 1994 within Ischigualasto Provincial Park in San Juan, Argentina.
This creature lived alongside early dinosaurs such as Eoraptor, Herrerasaurus, Chromogisaurus, and Panphagia.
The paleoenvironment of the Ischigualasto Formation was a volcanically active alluvial plain covered by forests and subject to heavy seasonal rains.
Phylogenetic analysis classifies Sanjuansaurus as a herrerasaurid dinosaur belonging to the parent group Herrerasauridae and the family Herrerasauridae.
It is further classified in the class Saurischia.

Fossil evidence dates Sanjuansaurus to approximately 231.4 million years ago during the late Carnian Stage, though the time range for the genus spans from 237 to 227.3 million years ago, placing it at the end of the Ladinian during the Middle Triassic or the Late Triassic.
Sanjuansaurus lived in South America approximately 231 million years ago during the Carnian stage of the Middle Triassic, inhabiting the Late Triassic jungles of the continent.
